for: Quarterdeck build PR 7, Mail content: To and Cc on every mail, many bots in one thread, a forward linked both ways
author: Quarterdeck contributors
how: Example data. Merge by reference. 'ccAdd' gives the Cc list of every existing mail, by mail reference: set it as 'cc' on that mail in data.js mail (MT-101 to MT-104) and in bots.json mailAdd (MT-105). A mail's 'to' and 'from' stay as they are. An empty list means no one was copied. There is no Bcc field anywhere.

'threadsAdd' lists two new threads in data.js mail shape (ref, subject, projectId, laneId, cardId, bots, mails) with 'cc' on every mail. Append them to the mail list. MT-106 is the forward of MT-101.2; MT-107 is the thread with four bots. 'bots' is the set of bots in the thread (alphabetical, as data.js has it); the order to show is 'botsOrdered' in 'expected.threads'.

A thread's bots are every bot that sent, received or was copied on any of its mails. Their display order is first appearance, reading the mails in order and each mail as From, then To, then Cc (the order the flow and preview m3 draw). The Mac list row shows the first two names and '+N' for the rest; the thread header lists them all. 'expected.threads[ref].listRow' holds both.

'forwardedFrom' on a mail (MT-106.1) names the mail it forwards; its quoted text, writer, recipient and time come from that mail. 'forwardedBy' on the original (MT-101.2) names who forwarded it, to whom and where (the ruling, flow step 4). 'expected.forward' holds the lines both ways.

'existingMailFixes' is the one change to an existing mail field other than cc and forwardedBy: MT-101.2 'artifactRefs' becomes [] (it was ['AR-1']). MT-101.2 is from 8:20 AM and AR-1 is added by data.js at 9:05 AM, so the mail cannot link it yet. Set it on that mail in data.js. The 9:05 AM Activity line in Lane Search still links AR-1 with MT-101.2, so nothing else moves.

'expected' is computed from the merged data so a build can check itself: bot order and row, day headings and list order (newest last mail first, the ruling: Today, Yesterday, then one heading per earlier day), the To line, Cc line, quote header and Ask list of every mail, and the bot filter (a bot matches when it sent, received or was copied, the ruling).

Ask list: the writer first marked '(wrote it)', then the thread's other bots in thread order, then 'Another bot...'. A removed bot (Pib) is not listed and gets '(removed)' beside its name where it is named (flow 'A removed bot', US-23).

Times are ISO in New York time, -04:00 before Sun Nov 1, 2026, 2:00 AM and -05:00 after, as in data.js mail. Every time is at or before 'now'. No bot's mail is later than that bot's lastActiveAt in bots.json; no mail reaches Pib after it was removed.
Nothing here edits a Lane, a card, a Page, an Artifact or a chat. MT-105 is as bots.json has it; only its Cc is added here.

openCalls: Bot order: data.js lists each thread's bots alphabetically, but the flow and preview m3 order them by first appearance (writer, then To, then Cc). This file follows the flow and gives 'botsOrdered'. For MT-102 the header reads 'Shelvorn, Iris', not 'Iris, Shelvorn'; for MT-103 'Alba, Shelvorn, Iris'. The design lead's call.
An empty Cc: the ruling says every mail shows 'cc <bots>'. For an empty Cc this file suggests drawing no cc line at all (not 'cc' with nothing). The design lead's call.
Removed bot: '(removed)' is suggested beside Pib's name wherever it is named (To line, Cc line, thread header), as the flow draws it for the writer. The design lead's call.
Earlier-day heading: the ruling says 'Today, Yesterday and earlier day headings'. This file writes 'Fri Oct 30'. The design lead's call.
Thread-header Ask (the ruling gives the writer-first list for a single mail only): suggested list is every bot in the thread in thread order, then 'Another bot...'. The design lead's call.

MT-106 has cardId null. MT-101 already sits behind alba-1, and the card's Mail tile points at one thread; a second thread on the same card could break a one-thread assumption. The forward links back to MT-101.2 instead.
Cc choices on the existing mails (MT-101.3, MT-101.4 and MT-103.1) are content calls made here, using only bots already in each thread, so no thread's bot list changes.
